newsitem.title: USA: Ill. lawmaker plans hearing on Tollway spending.
newsitem.headline: Ill. lawmaker plans hearing on Tollway spending.

text.p: An Illinois House committee will review next week Illinois State Toll Highway Authority spending in response to a court finding that its budgeting system lacked constitutional authority, the committee chairman announced Monday.

The House Appropriations Committee for General Services and Government Oversight will convene July 16 in Chicago with the House Appropriations Committee for Public Safety to review the Toll Authority's spending practices, said Rep. Jeff Schoenberg, D-Evanston.

The state court ruling prompted Moody's Investors, Standard & Poor's and Fitch Investors to raise possible negative implications for the Toll Authority's approximately $979 million of outstanding debt.
The trustee of the bonds, First National Bank of Chicago, a unit of First Chicago NBD Corp, has intervened in the ongoing dispute.

While confident in their own budgets, officials from the Illinois Development Finance Authority, Illinois Educational Facilities Authority and Illinois Housing Development Authority have said they are closely following the litigation to see if it could affect them also.
"A legislative solution must be carefully and deliberately charted to be financially responsible and to construct a fiscal firewall surrounding the Toll Highway Authority bonds," Schoenberg said.
Cook County Judge Stephen Schiller found in May that the Toll Authority's budget practices failed to meet requirements.
Schiller entered a preliminary injunction last month and stayed its effect until December 15 to give the General Assembly an opportunity to adopt a budget and the Toll Authority time to appeal.
